steps.what: Agree vulnerability assessment scope, owners, availability and required outputs
Populate the assessment schedule, tracker and invitation drafts
Resolve coordination conflicts and send checked assessment arrangements

tasks.design: Use {CALENDAR} and {PROJECT} templates to populate draft arrangements from the engineer's agreed scope and availability. The engineer resolves conflicts and sends the checked version; the workflow neither starts a scan nor expands assessment authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed assessment details can be repeatedly copied into invitations and trackers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reuse explicit coordination fields.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling operational constraints and deciding who can authorise the assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer understands why a proposed time or scope is unsuitable.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicated coordination entry while scope and operational agreement remain human.

reach.learn: Describe scope, outputs and operational constraints precisely

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: calendar and project templates can populate agreed assessment arrangements without choosing scope or authorising technical testing.

assumptions: Boundary is coordination, excluding vulnerability scanning, findings analysis and remediation performed under separate authority.

Engineer captures assessment ID, target list, scope version, owners, participants, selected time window, availability snapshot and required outputs in s1's 45 hours. Existing owners supply availability and constraints during that consultation; missing fields cause manual coordination, not inferred readiness. S2 only formats the selected arrangement.
Test native calendar and tracker configuration before code; savings require actual repeated entry rather than existing runtime.
No new status-reporting duty is imposed on assessment staff; any later new tracking capture must be separately costed.
unknowns: Current duplicate invitation or tracker entry
research_questions: Does a dry-run coordination package preserve scope and participants while reducing repeated entry?

approvals.approved_version: Exact coordination package version, scope, recipients, selected window and required outputs checked before sending; changed arrangements require fresh approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70, gross=30 and net=24 after six upkeep hours. Range assumes partly manual duplicate coordination entry; scope discussions and conflict resolution keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review security assessments against applicable criteria

steps.what: Identify assessment evidence and applicable security criteria or obligations
Compare explicit assessment evidence values with mapped criteria
Review assessment quality, contextual controls and compliance uncertainties
Document review conclusions and route unresolved standards or regulatory questions

tasks.design: Use a native {OTHER} security assessment tool to compare only explicitly mapped evidence values with selected criteria. The engineer evaluates adequacy, compensating controls and uncertain applicability in {DOCS}; the comparison table is not a compliance certificate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exact criterion-to-evidence comparisons may be repeated manually across assessments.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured comparison tables can reuse versioned mappings.
tasks.still_hard: Stale evidence, context-dependent controls and unclear regulatory applicability.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises when a nominal match does not establish an effective control.
tasks.altitude: Less mechanical comparison while review conclusions and escalations remain human.

reach.learn: State the affected environment, evidence and unresolved obligation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit evidence comparators can support a security review, but cannot determine contextual control adequacy or legal compliance.

assumptions: Boundary is reviewing an existing assessment; conducting the assessment, remediation and statutory reporting are separate work. National obligations are confirmed locally.

Assessment owner supplies evidence IDs, values, source references and dates as existing assessment work. Engineer selects baseline version, criterion IDs, exact field mappings, expected values and comparators in s1's 25 hours. Missing evidence or criteria needing interpretation remain unassessed and are examined manually in s3, with additional failures counted in upkeep.
Try native assessment reporting before custom code; savings require observed manual exact-value comparisons, not existing scanner or rule runtime.
No generated compliant flag or automatic release of the review is introduced.
unknowns: Share of criteria supporting exact comparisons
Quality and freshness of assessment evidence
research_questions: Can configured comparisons reproduce manual results while exposing every criterion requiring contextual review?

incremental.description: Criteria mapping updates and unsupported-evidence exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20 and net=14 after six upkeep hours. Range assumes a modest exact-comparison burden; applicability and control effectiveness judgement retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collect fault symptoms and relevant network or security evidence
Diagnose possible causes and draft a correction hypothesis

loop.purpose: Draft evidence-linked fault explanations and a bounded correction candidate
loop.input: Selected redacted symptoms, telemetry, configuration and runbook extracts
loop.output: At most three explanations and one candidate correction with supporting observations
loop.check: Engineer verifies each explanation against original evidence and reproduces the fault; independent tests must demonstrate the candidate addresses the fault while preserving required protection
loop.stop: One draft; missing evidence, uncertain interfaces or inability to test returns to manual diagnosis, with no scanning or execution by the model
loop.why_not_simpler: Known faults use runbooks and native filters; unfamiliar free-text symptoms across systems may require a provisional semantic explanation

steps.what: Test the candidate correction in a safe isolated environment
Approve and apply the exact tested correction
Verify fault resolution and retained security protection

tasks.design: Use native {OTHER} diagnostics and existing {DOCS} runbooks first, with a bounded hypothesis draft only for unfamiliar faults. The engineer reproduces the problem, tests the correction and approves application; restored connectivity alone does not establish preserved security.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unfamiliar faults can require repeated reading across symptoms and configuration.
tasks.enabler_now: Read-only drafting can propose explanations for independent engineering tests.
tasks.still_hard: A quick fix can mask a cause or weaken a necessary control.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer checks both service recovery and the intended protection boundary.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass hypothesis writing while troubleshooting and change responsibility stay human.

reach.learn: Test connectivity and protection as separate outcomes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound diagnostic drafts can suggest hypotheses, but network and security corrections require reproduction and independent protection checks.

assumptions: Boundary is reactive fault diagnosis and correction, excluding planned software installation and formal breach investigation; overlapping work is allocated once.

Engineer captures fault ID, environment, timestamps, selected event references, relevant configuration versions and observed symptoms in s1's 25 hours. Existing monitoring produces raw telemetry, not a root-cause label. Missing context stops drafting for manual diagnosis; source selection and redaction are counted in s1.
Try native diagnostics and runbooks before a model; existing telemetry or test runtime earns no saving.
Drafting has no credentials, production control or permission to change security settings; changes follow the engineer's existing authority.
research_questions: Do reviewed hypotheses reduce diagnosis effort after counting false leads and protection regression tests?

incremental.description: Diagnostic context upkeep and rejected-hypothesis handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested correction hash or configuration version, targets, fault and protection test evidence and rollback version; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=89.5, gross=10.5 and net=5.5 after five upkeep hours. Range assumes useful unfamiliar-fault drafts; evidence capture, testing, correction and verification retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate security policy and test documentation

steps.what: Collect owner documents and record exact security documentation references
Assemble the security documentation index and evidence package
Check documentation coverage and coordinate unresolved owner revisions

tasks.design: Configure a {DOCS} index and package template from engineer-confirmed document references. The engineer still obtains the inputs, checks substantive coverage and resolves gaps with owners; assembly does not approve or publish a policy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document references can be copied repeatedly into indexes and evidence packages.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates can reuse explicit owner, version and evidence links.
tasks.still_hard: A present document may not address the intended policy or test requirement.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises substantive gaps and obtains the appropriate owner's revision.
tasks.altitude: Less packaging and indexing while documentation coordination and meaning checks remain human.

reach.learn: Bind source references to exact versions and owners

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a fixed documentation index can be assembled from explicit source references without judging policy adequacy or drafting its substantive rules.

assumptions: Boundary is documentation coordination and package preparation, excluding authoring policies, executing tests and formal publication or approval.

Existing policy, procedure and test owners produce their documents as unchanged work. Engineer captures document ID, exact version, owner, requirement association, source link and evidence date in s1's 35 hours. Missing or inconsistent references remain gaps for manual enquiry; no approved-policy or adequate-test flag is inferred.
Test native document indexes and templates before code; savings require actual manual packaging or duplicate indexing, not existing repository runtime.
No new structured-capture duty is transferred to document owners; the engineer's manifest capture is fully counted.
research_questions: Can the generated package preserve every selected source version while making missing references visible?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65, gross=35 and net=29 after six upkeep hours. Range assumes partial manual package assembly; source collection, substantive checks and owner coordination retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated coordination entry, exact comparisons and document packaging while retaining assessment judgement and tested fault correction.
reach: Maintain versioned documentation indexes with records specialists
skills_to_grow: Capture exact scope and source versions
role.ambitious_version: A security engineer who can coordinate traceable assessments and documentation with fewer duplicate entries and clear human ownership of conclusions.
